title: After switching audio devices using the radio buttons, sometimes both the old and new devices' buttons get stuck in a "selected" state
line: After unplugging the current audio device, the Audio Volume widget no longer ends up with two devices selected or a device that can't be picked.
explanation: When the default device disappeared, pulseaudio-qt announced the default change from the map's removed signal, which runs before the models finish removing the row (the Server connects first). The applet's radio buttons re-read their device through the proxy model in that window, got nothing for rows after the removed one, and their 'PulseObject?.default' bindings stopped tracking the device for good. Such a row then kept whatever state the user clicked it into, leaving two devices checked, and clicking it again did nothing because a checked radio button doesn't toggle. The server now clears a default device when its row is about to be removed, before the models start the removal, so views always see consistent rows.

commits.message:
server: drop a removed default device before its row goes away

Removing the default device announced the default change while models
were halfway through removing its row, so applet radio buttons could
lose track of their device and stay checked; clear it beforehand now.

BUG: 500968

media.caption: Pure master: HDMI (default) unplugged and plugged back, then Headphones and Speakers picked: both stay selected
Same steps with the fix: only Speakers is selected
Pure master: replug HDMI, pick Headphones, Speakers, then Headphones again: Headphones stays selected and can no longer be picked (default stays Speakers)
Same steps with the fix: the selection always follows the click, and picking Headphones again works

reviews.text: Clearing a removed default sink or source in Server on MapBaseQObject::aboutToBeRemoved instead of removed fixes the real root cause in pulseaudio-qt: default-change notifications no longer fire between beginRemoveRows() and endRemoveRows() when proxy/view indices are inconsistent and corrupt QML PulseObject?.default bindings. The patch is minimal, lifetime-safe, and convincingly verified with before/after videos, stress testing, and passing autotests.

The diagnosis is sound and in the right layer. Server is built before any model, so its 'removed' slot ran after m_data.removeAt but before the models' endRemoveRows. A defaultSinkChanged sent in that window made delegates read shifted rows, and the 'PulseObject?.default' binding lost its dependency for good. That also explains the reports that only one widget instance gets stuck (c32/c37) and the trigger after unplugging USB or Bluetooth devices (c35/c36). Clearing the default in aboutToBeRemoved, before beginRemoveRows, keeps views consistent, and the reset() and replug paths still resolve through 'added' and server-info updates. The before/after shots and the pactl-checked stress loop are convincing, and the earlier no-op-backend cause was already fixed by 1af59b54.
